Grievance Redressal
A Grievance Redressal Cell, is in place, to look into the grievances of Students and Employees of the College.  It consists of the Principal, Dean-Operations and Senior Professors.  Grievances which are brought to the notice, of the concerned, are addressed suitably.  If necessary, the issues will be escalated to the Management.
The GRC shall meet at least once in each semester or as and when necessary.
The College has the following Mechanism for Grievance Redressal.
i.	 Mechanisms for Redressal of General Grievances
1.	The Students express their grievances, if any, in Virtual [Online], Mode through the College Website or submit a written complaint through their designated Mentors.  Also, a Complaint/ Suggestion Box, secured with a lock, is placed near the Reception where any Stakeholder can deposit the Complaint.  The Complaint Box is checked on the previous day of the Heads of the Department (Normally first Wednesday of every month), by the Personnel of the Office of the Principal.
2.	The Grievance Redressal Cell shall take appropriate Action on the complaint.
3.	After Investigation and/or Enquiry, the Committee resolves the issue impartially and confidentially. In some rare cases, it may escalate the issue to the Management for advisory and decision.
ii.	Mechanisms for Redressal of Grievances connected to the University
1.	If a Student is not satisfied with Awarded Marks/Grades in the University Examination, he/she can apply:
a.	On-line, for revaluation of his/her Answer Script after paying the prescribed fee.
b.	The Student can, also, apply for a Photocopy of his/her Answer Script. The Photocopy will be mailed to the E-Mail Address, provided by the Student.
c.	If the Results, post-revaluation are not satisfying, then the aggrieved Students can apply, challenging the Revaluation.

Examination-Coordinator of the respective Department will assist the Students in getting their Grievances for these options.
2.	 For problems such as Printing Errors in Grade Cards, issued by the University, Complaints are forwarded by the College Office, to the University, for correction.
iii.	 Mechanism for Redressal of Grievances with reference to Evaluation at College Level
1.	After each Internal Assessment Examination, evaluated Answer Books are shown to the Students by the Course Faculty.  The Scheme of Evaluation and the expected answers are, also explained to them. Health Center
Health Centre
Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan is committed to ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of students,
      faculty, and staff through a well-established on-campus Health Centre. The institution recognizes that a healthy
      campus environment is essential for effective learning, productivity, and overall well-being.
The Health Centre functions as the first point of medical support within the campus and is equipped to handle
      routine health needs, minor illnesses, and emergency first aid.
Medical Facilities & Staffing
Full-Time Nursing Support
The Health Centre is staffed with a dedicated full-time qualified nurse who is available on campus during working hours to:
Provide immediate first aid and basic medical care
Attend to minor injuries, cuts, burns, sprains, and fever
Monitor students who feel unwell during academic hours
Maintain health records and first-aid inventory
Doctor on Call
The institution has an arrangement with a qualified medical doctor on call, ensuring:
Medical consultation whenever required
Timely medical advice for cases needing expert attention
Support during medical emergencies until further referral
Tie-Up with Multi-Speciality Hospital
Navkis College of Engineering has a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a nearby multi-speciality
        hospital to provide advanced medical support beyond campus facilities.
This collaboration ensures:
Priority medical consultation and treatment
Emergency care and hospitalization if required
Access to specialist doctors and diagnostic facilities
Seamless referral during medical emergencies
Services Offered
First Aid & Emergency Care
Immediate response to injuries and sudden illness
Stabilization of patients before referral
Preliminary Medication
Basic medicines for common ailments such as fever, cold, headache, stomach discomfort, and minor infections
Administration of prescribed medication under supervision
Health Monitoring & Support
Blood pressure and basic health checks
Observation and rest facilities for students feeling unwell
Emergency Coordination
Rapid communication with the doctor on call
Immediate referral to the partnered hospital when necessary
Student Safety & Well-Being
The Health Centre plays a vital role in:
Ensuring student safety during academic hours, laboratory sessions, sports, and events

Organizational Structure
Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan (NCEH) follows a well-defined and transparent organizational structure 
            that ensures effective governance, academic leadership, administrative efficiency, and quality assurance.

            enabling smooth institutional functioning.

            compliance, and continuous quality improvement, in alignment with AICTE, VTU, and UGC guidelines.

            direction, policy oversight, and long-term vision for the institution. The Governing Council ensures that 
            institutional goals are aligned with regulatory requirements, academic standards, and societal needs.

            implementing the policies and decisions of the Governing Council. The Principal is supported by academic 
            leaders, administrative heads, and functional coordinators to ensure efficient institutional operations.

Outreach, Extension & Social Engagement
Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan (NCEH) believes that technical education must extend beyond classrooms
      and laboratories to address real societal challenges. The institution’s Outreach and Extension activities are

To apply engineering knowledge for societal benefit
To foster social responsibility, empathy, and civic consciousness among students
To support rural development, health, education, and sustainability initiatives
To strengthen campus–community linkages through long-term engagement

Outreach activities at NCEH are implemented through a well-defined structure:
Strategic oversight by the Principal
Quality monitoring and documentation by IQAC
Execution through Cells, Clubs, Committees, and Departments
Active participation of faculty coordinators and student volunteers

This initiative enables “learning by teaching”, benefiting both students and communities.

Scholarships & Financial Assistance
Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan (NCEH) is committed to ensuring inclusive and equitable access to quality
      education by supporting students through a wide range of government, AICTE, and institutional scholarship schemes.
      The institution has a well-defined Scholarship Facilitation and Monitoring Framework to ensure transparency,
      timely processing, and effective utilization of scholarships.
Scholarships at NCEH are aligned with student-centric policies, focusing on merit, socio-economic background,
      special achievements, and inclusivity.
Government & AICTE Scholarship Schemes
Students of NCEH are supported under the following Government of India and Government of Karnataka scholarship
        schemes, subject to eligibility criteria prescribed by the respective authorities:
Major Scholarship Schemes
Post Matric Scholarship
Departments: Social Welfare, Tribal Welfare, Minority Welfare
Eligibility: SC/ST/Minority students, annual family income as per norms
Merit-cum-Means Scholarship
Departments: Department of Education (DTE), Technical Education Department
Eligibility: Meritorious students from economically weaker sections
Defence Scholarship
Departments: Defence Ministry / State Government
Eligibility: Children of armed forces personnel
Fee Concession Scheme
Departments: Backward Class Welfare / Agriculture Department
Eligibility: Category-based, income criteria applicable
Food & Accommodation Scholarship
Departments: State Government / Educational Institutions
Eligibility: Students facing financial hardship
National Scholarship Portal (NSP) Schemes
Department: Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India
AICTE Pragati Scholarship (for Girls)
AICTE Saksham Scholarship (for Differently Abled Students)
AICTE – National Doctoral Fellowship (NDF)
Swanath Scholarship Scheme
Eligibility: Orphans, wards of parents who died due to COVID-19, wards of martyrs
Institutional Scholarship Schemes
In addition to government scholarships, NCEH provides Institutional Scholarships to support deserving students
        through an Institutional Scholarship Committee, ensuring fairness and accountability.

Merit-Based Scholarship

Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan (NCEH)
follows a structured, institution-wide Mentoring and 
            Counselling System aimed at supporting students’ academic progress, emotional well-being, personal 
            development, and career readiness. The system is designed as a proactive, faculty-led support mechanism 
            and is an integral part of the institution’s student-centric and outcome-oriented academic framework.
The mentoring framework functions in alignment with the Institutional Academic Calendar, departmental 
            plans, and quality assurance mechanisms coordinated by IQAC, ensuring continuity, accountability, and 
            continuous improvement.
Objectives of the Mentoring & Counselling System
Build strong and meaningful teacher–student relationships
Provide academic guidance and performance monitoring
Support students’ emotional, psychological, and social well-being
Facilitate smooth transition into engineering education, especially for first-year students
Identify and address academic or personal challenges at an early stage
Guide students towards career planning, higher education, and professional growth
Ensure a safe, inclusive, and supportive campus environment
Mentoring Framework & Process
Each faculty mentor is assigned a group of 20–25 students
Regular mentor–mentee meetings are conducted as per schedule
Academic progress, attendance, and mentoring interactions are documented through the DHI portal
Parents are kept informed periodically regarding academic progress and concerns
Issues requiring escalation are referred to the HoD, Counselling Cell, or specialized committees
The mentoring process is standardized through an approved Mentor–Mentee Handbook, ensuring uniformity 
            across departments.
Academic & Personal Support Initiatives
Support for Slow Learners
Identification through internal assessments and mentoring interactions
Remedial classes and focused academic counselling
Continuous monitoring and follow-up
Support for Advanced Learners
Advanced assignments and enrichment activities
Encouragement for certifications, projects, and competitions
Motivation towards research and higher studies
Counselling & Student Well-Being
Individual and group counselling sessions
Psychological and emotional support mechanisms

ABOUT US
Navkis College of Engineering (NCEH)
is a professionally governed technical institution committed to 
          academic excellence, ethical values, innovation, research orientation, and holistic student development.
Established in
2009–10
by the
Yagachi Education and Research Trust
, and functioning under the 
          patronage of the
Navkis Group of Institutions, Bengaluru since 2019–20
, the institution draws strength 
          from a strong educational legacy, progressive leadership, and a quality-driven governance framework.
The College is approved by
AICTE
, affiliated to
Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), Belagavi
, 
          and recognized under
Section 2(f) of the UGC Act
. All academic and administrative processes are carried out 
          in strict compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
Located in a serene and picturesque campus at Hassan, Navkis College of Engineering provides an intellectually 
          stimulating academic ambience supported by state-of-the-art infrastructure, modern laboratories, ICT-enabled 
          classrooms, robust digital systems, and comprehensive student support facilities.

Overview
The Career Guidance Cell (CGC) at Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan plays a pivotal role in enabling students to make informed and well-planned career decisions. The Cell supports students in identifying suitable career pathways across industry, higher education, research, and entrepreneurship. Working in close coordination with the Training & Placement Department, academic departments, and industry professionals, the CGC ensures that students are career-ready and future-focused.
Objectives of the Career Guidance Cell
To guide students in identifying career options aligned with their interests, aptitude, and academic strengths.
To create awareness about diverse career opportunities in core engineering, IT/ITES, higher studies, public sector, and entrepreneurship.
To bridge the gap between academic learning and industry expectations.
To help students develop clarity, confidence, and a long-term career vision.
Career Counselling & Mentoring
One-to-one and group career counselling sessions conducted by trained faculty mentors and Placement Team members.
Personalized guidance based on students’ academic performance, skill sets, and career aspirations.
Support for students in making informed career decisions at key academic and professional stages.
Guidance for Higher Studies & Competitive Examinations
Awareness sessions on higher education opportunities in India and abroad.
Guidance for competitive examinations such as GATE, GRE, TOEFL, IELTS, CAT, and other relevant entrance tests.
Mentoring support for university shortlisting, application processes, and preparation strategies.

Career talks and interactive sessions by industry professionals, alumni, and domain experts.
Orientation programs on emerging technologies, evolving job roles, and industry expectations.
Exposure to real-world career scenarios through seminars, webinars, and workshops.

Encouragement to pursue internships, certifications, online courses, and value-added programs aligned with career goals.

CHAIRMAN
MESSAGE
Welcome to Navkis College of Engineering and family of Navkis!
I extend my warmest greetings to you all. I welcome you to a new chapter in our quest to provide the best of education with a strong industry outlook through the unraveling of Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan. Embarking on this journey that started in 2000 through the first institution of Navkis in Bangalore, I am proud to say that the unwavering commitment, effort and experience of our teachers, parents and students have ensured Navkis to grow into a brand of quality and substance.
Carrying the torch lit by my father, Late Sri. M.S Ramaiah who set up the Ramaiah group of institutions, being one of the front runners in quality education in India, Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan aims at continuing this legacy.
I believe that education is the most powerful tool that can shape a country’s growth and its future. Hence, it is our responsibility as educators, to ensure that students are provided with a strong platform to build and nurture their skills and values in order to positively contribute to oneself and the social environment around them. Navkis College of Engineering Hassan aims at putting this thought to practice.
My vision for Navkis College of Engineering (NCE), Hassan, is to become a renowned engineering college to nurture agile and knowledgeable engineers.
Our core values of service, quality, innovation and harmony form the foundation for Navkis college of Engineering. We believe that today’s students are tomorrow’s leaders and therefore ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to equipping, exposing, enabling, empowering and enlightening our students. Here, students from rural, sub urban and tier 2 and 3 areas have access to a premium technical education institution in order to have a successful career ahead. Focusing on the three pillars of infrastructure, human resource and industry networks, we have ensured that students are provided a platform to aspire, achieve and excel.
Come and experience student life at Navkis and take a further step towards achieving your goal.
Shri. M. R. Anandram

E-Learning
Navkis College of Engineering - Hassan was quick to react to the pandemic situation that upset the entire education domain. Virtual sessions were started immediately during the lockdown and every single lecture was held using the Upswing platform. Online teaching was done continuously, videos recorded and shared and students went about answering all their assignments and tests using this platform.Both faculty and students quickly adapted to the new situation thus ensuring learning never stopped
Apart from this, the college has established facilities for technology enabled learning. There is facility for attending live E-Shikshana Courses offered by VTU. Students can watch the recorded video lectures also available on the VTU portal. There is a facility in every department for the Students and Faculty to watch the SWAYAM PRABHA channels. Lectures on subjects of importance by experts will be telecasted on 16 channels dedicated to different branches of study. The students can watch them during free time and enhance their knowledge. All Faculty and Students are encouraged to register for NPTEL (National Programme for Technology Enhanced Learning) courses on subjects of importance and recent technologies. Ms. Shruthi K. Oversee financial planning, infrastructure development, and resource allocation
Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, and accreditation requirements
Monitor institutional performance and governance effectiveness
Support innovation, research, and industry collaboration initiatives

Internship (VTU-Specific)
Internship is an integral part of the Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) curriculum and is made mandatory for all B.E./B.Tech students. It plays a vital role in enhancing the technical and professional competence of students and as an affiliated Institute we (NCEH) follow VTU and all our students are doing Internship through VTU Portal.
1. Mandatory Requirement as per VTU
VTU has included internships as a credit-based and compulsory component of the academic program.
Successful completion of the internship is required for the award of the degree.
2. Industry Exposure
VTU internships provide students with:
Exposure to real-time industry practices
Understanding of industrial standards, tools, and technologies
Practical experience beyond classroom learning
This prepares students for professional engineering roles.
3. Application of Theoretical Knowledge
Internships help VTU students apply:
Engineering theories
Laboratory concepts
Core subject knowledge
to solve real-world engineering problems, improving conceptual clarity.
4. Skill Development
VTU internships focus on developing:
Technical skills relevant to the student’s branch
Soft skills such as communication, teamwork, and discipline
Professional ethics and workplace behavior
These skills are essential for career growth.
5. Academic and Career Benefits
Internships help VTU students in:
Choosing suitable career paths or specializations
Improving employability and placement readiness
Gaining experience useful for competitive exams and higher studies
6. Support for Final-Year Project
Many VTU students:
Identify industry-oriented project topics
Receive practical guidance from industry mentors
Improve the quality and relevance of final-year projects
7. Evaluation and Credit System
As per VTU norms:
Internship performance is evaluated through reports, diaries, and certificates
Credits are awarded based on satisfactory completion
Non-completion may delay academic progression
8. Enhances Placement Opportunities
Internship experience:
Strengthens resumes for campus placements
Increases chances of Pre-Placement Offers (PPOs)
Builds confidence during technical and HR interviews
Thus, the internship program prescribed by VTU plays a crucial role in bridging the gap between academics and industry, ensuring holistic development of engineering graduates.

IoT Skill Lab
The IoT Skill Lab at Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan is a dedicated, state-of-the-art facility
      established by the Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering to provide hands-on, experiential
      learning in the rapidly evolving domain of the Internet of Things (IoT). The lab bridges the gap between
      theory and practice by enabling students to design, build, and test real-world IoT systems.
Purpose & Vision
The IoT Skill Lab is designed to:
Equip students with industry-relevant IoT skills
Promote project-based and problem-based learning
Encourage innovation, critical thinking, and teamwork
Prepare learners for careers in IoT, smart systems, automation, and data-driven applications
Training Structure
The training is structured in progressive levels, aligned with the VTU Skill Lab framework and institutional curriculum.
Level 1 – Basic (Semester 3)
Focuses on fundamentals of IoT and microcontroller-based system design using Arduino.
Arduino Uno programming using Arduino IDE
Interfacing sensors and actuators
GPIO, PWM, displays, motors, and buzzers
Mini projects addressing real-world problems
Learning Outcome:
Students gain strong foundations in sensor interfacing, automation, and prototype development.
Level 2 – Intermediate (Semester 5)
Emphasizes connectivity, wireless communication, and cloud integration using NodeMCU and Raspberry Pi.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GSM, GPS interfacing
Cloud platforms for data publishing and visualization
Web-based device control and monitoring
Camera interfacing and advanced mini projects
Learning Outcome:
Students design connected systems with device-to-cloud and device-to-device communication.
Level 3 – Advanced
Training by external industry experts and vendors
Exposure to advanced IoT use cases and industrial practices
Orientation towards research, innovation, and startups
Major Equipment & Infrastructure
The IoT Skill Lab is equipped with modern hardware and tools, including:
Arduino Uno boards and Raspberry Pi kits
NodeMCU and wireless communication modules
Sensors: Temperature & Humidity, Gas, Soil Moisture, LDR, PIR, Ultrasonic
Actuators: DC, Servo, Stepper Motors, Relays
LCDs, buzzers, cameras, and measurement instruments
High-performance computing systems with internet connectivity
Teaching–Learning Approach
Demonstration-based and hands-on laboratory sessions
Mini-project-driven learning with societal and industrial relevance
Team-based experimentation, documentation, and presentations
Integration of cloud platforms and introductory AI/ML concepts for data analytics

DEPARTMENT OF PHYSICS
The Department of Physics was established in the year 2001 during the inception of the Institution. The department is devoted to teaching undergraduate students. The department of Physics, with its vision Integrating Physics with technology aims at providing a strong basement in scientific methods in applied physics. The department has well qualified and dedicated staff involved in research besides teaching.
Efficient teaching along with the best training in the laboratories are the highlights of the department. The department has a spacious and well equipped laboratory. The department provides required components and gadgets to students to try hands on experience in practical classes. The department is maintaining an aggregate of 90-95 % of result in Engineering Physics theory examination.
VISION
To produce high quality Engineers with strong knowledge in Engineering with
                          Physics that helps to develop latest technology. To motivate research interest in area of IT

MISSION
Department of Physics achieves its mission by trying to evenly represent the underlying

PRINCIPAL
MESSAGE
Welcome to our Navkis Engineering Institution.
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you to our institution, a place where knowledge, innovation, and values come together to shape the engineers and leaders of tomorrow. Our college is committed to providing quality technical education that empowers students with the knowledge, skills, and ethical values necessary to excel in a rapidly evolving global environment.
Engineering is not merely about acquiring technical knowledge; it is about solving real-world problems through creativity, innovation, and a commitment to excellence. At our institution, we strive to create an academic ecosystem that nurtures critical thinking, encourages research and innovation, and promotes lifelong learning. Our curriculum is complemented by modern laboratories, industry collaborations, internships, skill development programs, and project-based learning to ensure that our graduates are industry-ready and socially responsible.
We strongly believe that holistic education extends beyond the classroom. Students are encouraged to participate in co-curricular and extracurricular activities, professional societies, entrepreneurship initiatives, sports, cultural events, and community outreach programs. These experiences help develop leadership qualities, teamwork, communication skills, and a sense of social responsibility.
Our dedicated faculty members are committed to mentoring students and fostering an environment of academic excellence, integrity, and continuous improvement. We emphasize innovation, interdisciplinary learning, and collaboration with industry and research organizations to prepare our students for the challenges and opportunities of the future.
As we continue our journey towards academic excellence, we remain steadfast in our mission to produce competent engineers, innovative thinkers, ethical professionals, and responsible citizens who contribute meaningfully to society and nation-building.
I invite aspiring students, parents, alumni, industry partners, and all stakeholders to become a part of our vibrant academic community. Together, let us build a future driven by knowledge, innovation, and excellence.
I wish every student a rewarding educational journey filled with learning, discovery, and success.
Best Wishes
Dr Sanjay Pande MB

Department of Physical Education & Sports
The Department of Physical Education at Navkis College of Engineering, Hassan, firmly believes that sports and games are essential for the physical fitness, mental well-being, and overall personality development of students. As part of the Induction Programme, first-year students are introduced to Yoga and Meditation to promote concentration and a healthy lifestyle. The college provides excellent facilities for Athletics, Cricket, Volleyball, Football, Handball, Badminton, Throwball, Kho-Kho, Kabaddi, Table Tennis, Chess, and Carrom, along with expert coaching to prepare students for inter-collegiate, state, and national competitions. Students have consistently brought laurels to the institution through outstanding performances in tournaments conducted by Visvesvaraya Technological University and other state-level bodies, securing top positions in Volleyball, Handball, Throwball, Table Tennis, Karate, Gymnastics, Athletics, and Arm Wrestling. Several students have qualified for State, Inter-University, and National level championships, reflecting the college’s strong commitment to nurturing sporting excellence, leadership, discipline, and competitive spirit.
OBJECTIVE
To pursue excellence in the promotion and development of Physical Education and Sports through innovative coaching programmes and structured activities.
To adopt a holistic approach that ensures the harmonious development of body, mind, and spirit.
To design and implement innovative, integrated, and interdisciplinary curricula in Physical Education, sports, and allied areas.
To provide leadership and contribute meaningfully to the profession of Physical Education and Sports.
To actively promote fitness and health awareness among students, faculty, and the surrounding community.
To mould individuals into physically fit, emotionally mature, and socially responsible citizens.
ACHIEVEMENTS – OVERVIEW
The Department of Physical Education has consistently achieved remarkable success in various University, State, and National level competitions conducted by Visvesvaraya Technological University and other recognized sports bodie. Students have secured top positions in Volleyball, Handball, Throwball, Table Tennis, Karate, Gymnastics, Athletics, Arm Wrestling, and other sporting events. Several teams have emerged as Champions and Runners-up at divisional and state levels, while many individual players have won medals and qualified for Inter-University and National championships. These accomplishments reflect the department’s strong training system, expert coaching, and commitment to fostering excellence, discipline, and sportsmanship among students.

Training and Placement
The Training and Placement Department at NCEH plays a pivotal role in enhancing student employability and career progression by bridging the gap between academic learning and industry expectations. We are committed to providing systematic training, career guidance, and placement support to enable students to acquire the knowledge, skills, and professional competencies required in the dynamic global workforce.
We focus on the holistic development of students through structured training programs in technical skills, aptitude, communication, and soft skills, along with exposure to industry practices through internships, industrial training, and interaction with industry professionals. It actively collaborates with reputed organizations, industries, and institutions to facilitate internships, campus placements, and career opportunities.
Aligned with current industry requirements and student expectations, the Training and Placement Department ensures inclusive participation, equal opportunity, and continuous monitoring of student outcomes. By fostering industry–academia interaction, promoting professional ethics, and supporting lifelong learning, the department contributes significantly to the institution’s mission of producing competent, responsible, and employable engineering graduates.
Vision:
To empower students with relevant and conceptualized professional skills and to guide them towards a bright career, built on the values of sincerity, hard work, and justice.
Mission:
To strengthen and enhance Industry–Institute partnerships through effective campus connect initiatives, enabling students to gain practical exposure and industry-ready skills.
To maximize placement opportunities for all eligible students by establishing strong and sustainable relationships with leading industry stakeholders, thereby facilitating successful career pathways.
Objectives:
Student Support
To organize training programs on aptitude, technical skills, soft skills, and communication to enhance student employability.
To provide career counseling, mentoring, and guidance for placements, higher studies, and competitive exams.
To ensure access to training and placement support for all students, including economically and socially disadvantaged groups.
Student Progression
To facilitate placements, internships, apprenticeships, and industrial training through industry collaboration.
To encourage and guide students toward higher education, professional certifications, and entrepreneurship.
To track student progression in terms of placement, higher studies, and self-employment.
